name: Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses

raw_payload.title: Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses
raw_payload.summary: Byte-level language models such as the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) group bytes into patches and run their large global model once per patch. BLT starts a patch where a small model's next-byte entropy is high. We show that under tight patch budgets this rule has a blind spot: positions whose type the preceding text fixes but whose value must be computed, such as the number after "= " in a worked math solution. A nearly certain digit keeps the next byte's entropy near or below log2(10) = 3.32 bits, about BLT-1B's threshold for a 10% budget. In Meta's BLT-1B with patch starts on 10% of bytes, the entropy rule puts a patch start at 16% of the computed results in GSM8K solutions and gets 19.0% of them exactly right given the true preceding text; a boundary after each "=" at the same patch count gets 51.8%, and entropy combined with a label-free boundary-dependence signal gets 67.1% (default layout at 26% of bytes: 76.8%). The gap survives adapting BLT-1B to the budget with low-rank adapters (32.9% vs 72.7%, three runs per rule). In byte models trained from scratch at a 10% budget on a 1.9 GB math corpus, it is not detectable at 1M parameters, appears on final answers at 12M and on both targets at 50M, as training data grow too: at 50M boundary dependence gets 35.9% of computed results against 13.9% for entropy and 78.9% of final answers against 59.0% (3 seeds each), although final answers mostly copy the solution's last number and entropy starts a patch at every one. In BLT-1B the blind spot narrows at larger budgets (entropy covers about 90% of the values right after "= " at 20% of bytes) and in the same solutions rewritten as prose, where a patch start at each value still pays. Boundary dependence, the change in the model's own loss when a patch start is removed or added, measured per two-byte context on text in the same format, finds these positions without labels.
